title: Lesson 4: Building a Reusable Delivery Toolkit: Skill Packaging Done Right
description: The difference between a consultant who solves one client's problem and one who compounds every engagement into the next: turning the working capture discipline, eval suite, and guardrail set from Lessons 2 and 3 into packaged, loadable skills another consultant can run without relearning them.

questions.question: What makes a skill's description effective for a reusable toolkit?
options: It summarizes the full text of the skill
It names the situation that triggers loading it
It lists every supporting file bundled inside the folder
It names the client the skill came from
questions.explanation: The description is the only thing the agent sees when deciding whether to load the skill, so it must name the situation, not the content.

questions.question: When packaging an engagement into a reusable skill, what should you keep?
options: The client's names and specific data formats
The complete record of the original engagement
The transferable core, minus client detail
Only the parts that were difficult to build
questions.explanation: A reusable skill keeps the procedure that transfers and strips the client-specific detail, or the next engagement cannot put it to use.

questions.question: How much should a single reusable skill try to cover?
options: Everything the consultant needs on a project
A whole engagement from start to finish
Every tool the team uses across clients
questions.explanation: A skill scoped to one deliverable or decision stays loadable and easy to route, while a skill covering everything bloats the index and applies poorly.
